Population.evidence_source: Purposive sampling was used to recruit four gay men between the ages of 35 and 41 through placing advertisements at the premises of voluntary organizations that support gay men. All participants experienced suicidality on at least one occasion during their adolescent years and had 'come out' in terms of identifying themselves as gay.

Type.evidence_source: While everything was done to promote a safe and sensitive environment for a face-to-face research encounter, alternative, less intrusive methods of data collection could have been considered, for example, digital storytelling. Such approaches could have yielded more participants. However, in narra- [/page/2/Text/3] tive research there is no fixed sample size, the focus being on the ideographic rather than the nomothetic in gaining greater understanding of the lived experience (Holloway & Freshwater 2007). In the context of this study, it is the richness of data rather than sample size that matters. Likewise, it is authenticity and resonation with findings from other studies rather than generalizability that should be considered. Authenticity was achieved through the in-depth analysis of each narrative followed by the analysis and synthesis of similarities across all four case studies and resonation through links to previous studies.
